summary: Kedlaya and Liu build relative p-adic Hodge theory on Witt vectors and nonarchimedean analytic geometry. They compare the Gel’fand spectra of Banach rings with Huber adic spectra, set up the perfectoid correspondence between perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebras and perfectoid algebras (compatible with rational localization and finite étale covers), and prove slope theory over relative Robba rings, including semicontinuity of the slope polygon and a slope filtration theorem. They relate ϕ-modules over relative Robba rings to vector bundles on relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and to étale Z_p- and Q_p-local systems on perfectoid and analytic spaces, with (pro-)étale cohomology. This is a partial extraction: two checkpoints cover the introduction and chapters 1–7, 228 items (18 library, 108 planned, 102 missing). Chapters 1–3 give algebraic preliminaries, spectra of Banach rings and the perfectoid correspondence. Mathlib has much of the commutative algebra, the seminorm theory, perfect rings, Witt vectors of perfect rings, inverse perfection and Fontaine’s θ. The Huber-ring and adic-spectrum material is planned in the Tau Ceti AdicSpaces roadmap (layers 0–4); the Gel’fand spectrum in TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0; the perfectoid correspondence, tilting of adic spectra and almost purity in PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3, which name this paper as a source; henselian-pair and finite étale inputs in P5; Beauville–Laszlo patching in RelativeFarguesFontaine RF4. Missing from chapters 1–3 are some commutative algebra (Fitting ideals, descent of projectivity, the trace criterion), the étale local systems and pro-étale site of a scheme (§1.4), the Gel’fand–adic comparison, affinoid systems, finite étale descent along rational coverings, glueing squares and Kiehl glueing for vector bundles on sheafy rings, the uniform-ring results of §2.8, Katz’s correspondence between lisse sheaves and ϕ-modules over a perfect ring, the Gauss norms on Witt vectors, the functoriality and descent statements of the perfectoid correspondence, and preperfectoid algebras. Chapter 4 reviews Kedlaya’s slope theory over the Robba ring and the extended Robba ring of a perfect analytic field, all planned in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0–RD.2. Chapter 5 builds the relative extended Robba rings of a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra and proves their sheaf and Kiehl-glueing properties, relative perfectoidness and finite étale functoriality; only the lifting of rational localizations and almost purity are planned (RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y, PerfectoidSpaces P0 and P3). Chapter 6 identifies ϕ-modules over these rings with ϕ-bundles and with vector bundles on Proj of the graded ring of Frobenius eigenvectors, planned in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1–VB2 and RelativeFarguesFontaine RF1 and RF3. Chapter 7 studies slopes in families: rank and degree, pure models, openness of the pure locus, semicontinuity and boundedness of the slope polygon, and the slope filtration where the polygon is constant; VB4 plans semicontinuity and the constant-polygon filtration for perfectoid bases. The missing items go as sources to the existing layers that should own them, in nineteen routes. 53 mistakes are recorded for chapters 1–7. 31 are new, among them a false Corollary 2.5.13 (it needs A^+ = A°, as the paper’s own Remark 2.4.9 shows), a failing step in Remark 2.3.15(e), a reversed inclusion in the proof of Proposition 2.4.24, a gap in the proof of Proposition 3.5.9, a citation of Scholze’s covering conjecture to the wrong paper in Remark 3.1.17, a false description of the φ^a-invariants of the extended Robba ring in Lemma 4.2.10 (they are W(L^{φ^a})[p^{−1}], which is Q_p for a = 2 and L the completed perfection of F_p((t))), and wrong exponents in the proof of Proposition 6.2.4. The other 22 are already in the authors’ errata in part II, among them the false equivalence in Definition 2.8.1 and the incomplete proofs of Propositions 3.6.11 and 3.6.19.

prerequisites.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Nagoya Math. J. 209 (2013), 111–165
prerequisites.why: [87]: the maps λ and μ between the Gel’fand spectra of a perfect ring R and of W(R) (Lemmas 4.1–4.2), which underlie the perfectoid correspondence (§3.3), the closedness of principal ideals generated by primitive elements (Theorem 5.11), and Banach-ring lemmas cited in §§2.2–2.3 (Gauss norms, Lemma 1.20). Bhatt–Scholze, Henkel, Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Mihara, Berkovich, Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Gabber–Ramero, Katz (p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms), Scholze and Scholze–Weinstein are already cited by the atlas.

prerequisites.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, Astérisque 319 (2008), 259–301
prerequisites.why: [kedlaya-relative] in the paper’s bibliography, cited fourteen times in chapters 4–7: the slope filtration and Dieudonné–Manin statements over the extended Robba ring (Proposition 1.2.7, Theorems 1.6.5 and 1.7.1), faithfully flat descent of φ-modules (§3, Proposition 3.2.2, Theorems 3.1.2–3.1.3, which Remark 4.3.6 corrects in Proposition 3.3.2), and the successive approximation of Proposition 2.5.8 used in Proposition 7.3.6. The atlas does not cite it.

prerequisites.citation: R. Rodriguez, Preperfectoid algebras, PhD thesis, University of California, San Diego, 2014
prerequisites.why: Source of Theorem 5.3.9, which the paper attributes to Rodriguez with its proof: ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R are relatively perfectoid, so their adic Banach extensions are stably uniform and sheafy with the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties; the paper then deduces Kiehl glueing for the sheaf ℛ̃^{[s,r]} on Spa(R, R⁺) (Theorem 5.3.13). The atlas does not cite it. The eScholarship PDF returned HTTP 403 here, so the thesis itself was not read.

items.name: Finite projective modules: direct summands, finitely presented flat and pointwise free
items.statement: For a module M over a ring R, the following are equivalent: (a) M is finitely generated projective; (b) M is a direct summand of a finite free module; (c) M is finitely presented and pointwise free (M ⊗ R_p free for every maximal, equivalently every prime, ideal p); (c′) M is finitely presented and flat.

items.name: Finite projective modules via locally constant rank and Zariski-local freeness
items.statement: For M finitely generated over R, the following are equivalent to M being finite projective: (d) M is pointwise free of locally constant rank; (e) M is locally free, i.e. there are f_1, …, f_n generating the unit ideal with each M[f_i^{−1}] free. For R reduced, finitely generated of locally constant rank suffices.
items.locator: §1.1, Definition 1.1.2 (d)–(e) and the reduced case, pp. 11–12
items.note: Mathlib has the pieces for finitely presented M (rankAtStalk, Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk, Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers, Module.Free.away_of_finite_of_flat_of_rankAtStalk_constant) but not the equivalences for finitely generated M or the reduced case.

items.name: Fitting ideals detect finite projective modules of constant rank
items.statement: For M finitely presented, the Fitting ideals Fitt_i(M) are finitely generated, increasing, eventually equal to R, and commute with base change; M is finite projective of constant rank n iff Fitt_i(M) = 0 for i < n and Fitt_n(M) = R.
items.note: Neither library has Fitting ideals of modules.

items.name: Faithfully flat modules and their criterion by maximal ideals
items.statement: M is faithfully flat if it is flat and M ⊗_R N ≠ 0 for every nonzero R-module N; equivalently, injectivity is preserved on finite modules and M ⊗ N ≠ 0 for finite N ≠ 0. A flat ring map R → S is faithfully flat iff every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a maximal ideal of S (Lemma 1.1.4).
items.note: Mathlib defines faithful flatness by m·M ≠ M for maximal m, which is the criterion with finite test modules; Lemma 1.1.4 is iff_flat_and_proper_ideal for M = S (mS ≠ S exactly when m is contracted from a maximal ideal of S).

items.name: Étale maps and the tensor category FÉt(R)
items.statement: A ring map is étale if it is of finite presentation and formally étale (EGA IV 17.3.1); étale maps are stable under base change and composition and are exactly the flat, formally unramified, finitely presented ones. FÉt(R) is the category of finite étale R-algebras, with base change FÉt(R) → FÉt(S). Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is finite projective over R.
items.locator: §1.2, Definition 1.2.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 12–13
items.note: Finite étale is written [Algebra.Etale R S] [Module.Finite R S]; projectivity combines flatness with finite presentation.

items.name: The trace-pairing criterion for finite étale algebras
items.statement: An R-algebra S that is finite projective as an R-module is finite étale over R iff the trace pairing S → Hom_R(S, R), x ↦ (y ↦ Tr_{S/R}(xy)), is an isomorphism. A faithfully finite étale algebra is one of positive rank everywhere.
items.note: Mathlib has the trace form over fields (traceForm_nondegenerate) but not the criterion over rings; the paper uses it pointwise in Lemma 3.6.20.

items.name: Morphisms out of a finite étale algebra are idempotents
items.statement: For U ∈ FÉt(R) there is an idempotent e_{U/R} ∈ U ⊗_R U mapping to 1 under multiplication and killing its kernel. For any R-algebra V, ψ ↦ e_ψ = (1 ⊗ ψ)(e_{U/R}) is a bijection from R-algebra maps U → V to idempotents e ∈ U ⊗_R V for which Γ(e) : V → e(U ⊗_R V), x ↦ e(1 ⊗ x), is an isomorphism.
items.note: Neither library has the diagonal idempotent of a finite étale algebra or the description of Hom sets by idempotents; Mathlib has FÉt(R) (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale) but not its Galois-category structure.

items.name: Idempotents modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical
items.statement: Let I be contained in the Jacobson radical of R. (a) Distinct idempotents of R are not congruent modulo I. (b) For any integral extension S of R, IS is contained in the Jacobson radical of S.
items.note: Mathlib lifts idempotents only along nil kernels (existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent).

items.name: Full faithfulness of base change on finite étale algebras
items.statement: (a) If R → R′ is such that an element of an invertible R-module M generating M ⊗ R′ generates M, and for every S ∈ FÉt(R) each idempotent of S ⊗_R R′ comes from a unique idempotent of S, then FÉt(R) → FÉt(R′) is rank-preserving and fully faithful. (b) If I lies in the Jacobson radical of R and idempotents of S/IS lift to S for every S ∈ FÉt(R), then FÉt(R) → FÉt(R/I) is rank-preserving and fully faithful.
items.note: P5 plans the finite étale approximation and full faithfulness arguments through Gabber–Ramero.

items.name: Henselian pairs and Gabber’s root criterion
items.statement: A pair (R, I) with I in the Jacobson radical is henselian if simple roots modulo I of monic polynomials lift (equivalently, by Gabber, every monic f with f_0 ∈ I and f_1 ∈ R^× has a root in I); I-adically complete pairs are henselian.
items.note: Mathlib’s HenselianRing is the root-lifting form. The instance that I-adically complete pairs are henselian is IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (RingTheory/Henselian.lean, line 170), which the declaration index omits.

items.name: Henselian pairs: lifting coprime factorizations
items.statement: The paper’s definition: (R, I) is henselian if I lies in the Jacobson radical and every factorization f = gh in (R/I)[T] of a monic f ∈ R[T] into coprime monic factors lifts to R[T]; this is equivalent to the root criterion.
items.note: The equivalence with the root-lifting form is proved in Mathlib only for local rings (HenselianLocalRing.TFAE).

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a henselian pair (Gabber, Elkik)
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I), the base change functor FÉt(R) → FÉt(R/I) is a tensor equivalence.
items.note: P5 cites Gabber–Ramero 5.4.53 for exactly this input.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a direct limit
items.statement: For a direct system of rings R_i with limit R, base extension induces a tensor equivalence from the 2-colimit of the FÉt(R_i) to FÉt(R) (EGA IV 17.7.8 and 1.8.4.2).

items.name: Cofibred categories, descent data and effective descent morphisms
items.statement: For a functor F : 𝓕 → C, a pushforward of E along f is a universal morphism over f with source E; F is cofibred if pushforwards exist and compose. For f : X → Y in C with pushouts, a descent datum along f is M over Y with an isomorphism π_1^*M ≅ π_2^*M satisfying the cocycle condition on Y ⊔_X Y ⊔_X Y; f is an effective descent morphism if every descent datum comes from X and morphisms descend bijectively.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent for modules
items.statement: Every faithfully flat ring map R → S is an effective descent morphism for modules (extension of scalars is comonadic), Zariski covers being a special case. Along a faithfully flat R → S, a module is finite, and an algebra is étale (hence finite étale when finite), iff its base change to S is.
items.note: Mathlib states effective descent in comonadic form; the descent-datum form is a TODO in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Descent.lean.

items.name: Finite projective modules descend along faithfully flat maps
items.statement: Along a faithfully flat ring map R → S, an R-module M is finite projective iff S ⊗_R M is finite projective over S.
items.note: Mathlib records this as missing (module docstring of RingTheory/Etale/Descent.lean: descent of projectivity, Stacks 058B); flatness and finiteness descend, but finite presentation of modules does not yet.

items.name: The Beauville–Laszlo theorem
items.statement: Let t ∈ R be a non-zero-divisor with R t-adically separated and R̂ the t-adic completion. (a) For flat M, 0 → M → M[t^{−1}] ⊕ (M ⊗ R̂) → M ⊗ R̂[t^{−1}] → 0 is exact. (b) Finite projective modules over R[t^{−1}] and R̂ with an isomorphism over R̂[t^{−1}] glue uniquely to a finite projective R-module; R → R[t^{−1}] ⊕ R̂ is an effective descent morphism for finite projective modules.
items.locator: §1.3, Proposition 1.3.6, pp. 16–17; new proof in Remark 2.7.9, p. 58

items.name: Glueing data over an exact square of rings
items.statement: For a commuting square R → R_1, R_2 → R_12 with 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 exact, a glueing datum is (M_1, M_2, M_12) with isomorphisms M_i ⊗ R_12 ≅ M_12; its glued module is M = ker(M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12).
items.note: RF4 plans the algebraic patching argument for nonnoetherian rings.

items.name: Surjectivity lemma for finite glueing data
items.statement: For a finite glueing datum with M ⊗ R_1 → M_1 surjective: M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12 is surjective, M ⊗ R_2 → M_2 is surjective, and a finitely generated submodule M_0 ⊆ M already surjects onto M_1 and M_2.

items.name: Glueing of finite projective modules over an exact square
items.statement: If M ⊗ R_1 → M_1 is surjective for every finite projective glueing datum, then (a) M is finitely presented and M ⊗ R_i ≅ M_i, and (b) if moreover the image of Spec(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → Spec(R) contains Maxspec(R), M is finite projective.
items.note: A notational slip in the proof (finding E1).

items.name: Glueing of finite étale algebras over an exact square
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 1.3.9(b), FÉt(R) → FÉt(R_1) ×_{FÉt(R_12)} FÉt(R_2) is an equivalence.

items.name: Étale Z_p-, isogeny Z_p- and Q_p-local systems on a scheme
items.statement: On the small étale site of X, a lisse sheaf of Z/p^n-modules is a sheaf of flat Z/p^n-modules represented by a finite étale X-scheme; a Z_p-local system is an inverse system (T_n) of such with T_{n+1}/p^n ≅ T_n; isogeny Z_p-local systems form its isogeny category; a Q_p-local system is a descent datum in isogeny Z_p-local systems for the étale topology. Over X_fét the Z_p- and isogeny categories are the same, the Q_p-category in general not.

items.name: Local systems and representations of the étale fundamental group
items.statement: For X connected with geometric point x, Z_p-local systems are equivalent to continuous representations of π_1^ét(X, x) on finite free Z_p-modules, and isogeny Z_p-local systems to continuous representations on finite-dimensional Q_p-vector spaces; a tensor equivalence FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(B) induces equivalences of the Z_p- and isogeny categories of Spec A and Spec B, but not of Q_p-local systems.

items.name: Q_p-local systems need not come from isogeny Z_p-local systems
items.statement: Two copies of P^1_k glued along {0, ∞} carry a rank-one Q_p-local system (identity on one branch, multiplication by p on the other) that is not an isogeny Z_p-local system; descending V ⊕ τ^*V along the degree-2 étale cover gives an irreducible (non-normal) example. For X normal and noetherian, Z_p-ILoc(X) → Q_p-Loc(X) is an equivalence.

items.name: The lattice schemes L_m(T)
items.statement: For a Z_p-local system T on X and m ≥ 0, the functor of pairs (T′, ι) with ι : T_Y ⊗ Q_p ≅ T′ ⊗ Q_p and p^mι, p^mι^{−1} integral is represented by a finite étale X-scheme L_m(T); it carries a finite étale inclusion scheme I_m(T), a sum-of-lattices operation, and descent along faithfully finite étale covers.

items.name: Descent of isogeny Z_p-local systems along finite étale covers
items.statement: Every faithfully finite étale ring map R → R′ is an effective descent morphism for isogeny Z_p-local systems.
items.note: A notational slip in the proof (finding E2).

items.name: Weakly étale morphisms and the pro-étale site of a scheme
items.statement: f : Y → X is weakly étale if f and its diagonal are flat (e.g. ind-étale algebras). X_proét is the site of weakly étale X-schemes with fpqc coverings; U ↦ Map_cont(U, T) is a sheaf (the constant sheaf F_T), and locally constant sheaves are those locally of this form.

items.name: Local systems as locally free sheaves on the pro-étale site (Bhatt–Scholze)
items.statement: For any scheme X, Z_p-Loc(X) (resp. Q_p-Loc(X)) is equivalent to the category of locally free F_{Z_p}-modules (resp. F_{Q_p}-modules) of finite rank on X_proét.
items.note: Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, §6.8.

items.name: Local systems with coefficients in a finite extension
items.statement: For F finite over Q_p one defines o_F-, isogeny o_F- and F-local systems as the Q_p-objects with an o_F-action; for F = Q_{p^d} unramified these are Z_{p^d}-Loc(X), Z_{p^d}-ILoc(X), Q_{p^d}-Loc(X).

items.name: Semilinear ϕ-actions and ϕ-cohomology
items.statement: For a ring S with endomorphism ϕ, a semilinear ϕ-action on an S-module M is an isomorphism ϕ^*M ≅ M. H^0_ϕ(M) = ker(ϕ − 1), H^1_ϕ(M) = coker(ϕ − 1), H^i_ϕ = 0 for i ≥ 2; these are the Ext groups Ext^i(S, M) over the twisted polynomial ring S{ϕ}, computed by 0 → S{ϕ} → S{ϕ} → S → 0. For a ϕ^d-action, H^i_{ϕ^d}(M) = H^i_ϕ(M ⊕ ϕ^*M ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ (ϕ^{d−1})^*M); a finite projective M has a dual ϕ-module.
items.note: The ring S in Remark 1.5.6 is misprinted as R (finding E4).

items.name: Finitely generated ϕ-modules are quotients of free ϕ-modules
items.statement: If M is a finitely generated S-module with a semilinear ϕ-action, there is a finite free S-module F with a semilinear ϕ-action and a ϕ-equivariant surjection F → M; if M is finite projective, there is a finite projective ϕ-module N with M ⊕ N free.
items.note: The block-matrix proof (det D = 1) was checked; its “bottom left block” should read “top left block” (finding E3, corrected in part II).

items.name: Nonarchimedean seminorms on abelian groups, domination and equivalence
items.statement: A (nonarchimedean) seminorm on G is α : G → [0, ∞) with α(g − h) ≤ max{α(g), α(h)} and α(0) = 0; a norm if α(g) = 0 only for g = 0. α dominates α′ if α′ ≤ cα; mutual domination is equivalence.
items.note: Domination and equivalence are the inequalities themselves; Mathlib has no named relation for them.

items.name: Bounded, isometric and submetric homomorphisms
items.statement: For ϕ : G → H with seminorms α, β: ϕ is bounded if β∘ϕ ≤ cα for some c, isometric if β∘ϕ = α, and submetric if β∘ϕ ≤ α.

items.name: Strict and optimal homomorphisms of seminormed groups
items.statement: With the quotient seminorm ᾱ on image(ϕ), ϕ is strict if ᾱ and β are equivalent there, almost optimal if they coincide, and optimal if moreover lifts of minimal norm exist. Compositions of strict maps are strict when the first is surjective or the second injective.
items.note: Mathlib has strictness only topologically (Topology.IsStrictMap) and quotient maps of normed groups (NormedAddGroupHom.IsQuotient).

items.name: Separated completion of a seminormed group
items.statement: The separated completion Ĝ is the quotient of the Cauchy sequences by the kernel of lim α(g_i); G → Ĝ is isometric, and injective iff α is a norm.
items.note: Mathlib’s completion of a seminormed group is normed; the map is isometric (norm_coe) and injective for a norm (coe_injective, T0).

items.name: Submultiplicative, power-multiplicative and multiplicative seminorms
items.statement: On a ring: submultiplicative α(gh) ≤ α(g)α(h); power-multiplicative in addition α(g²) = α(g)²; multiplicative in addition α(1) = 1 and α(gh) = α(g)α(h). The trivial norm is power-multiplicative iff A is reduced and multiplicative iff A is a domain; a submultiplicative α dominates a power-multiplicative α′ iff α ≥ α′ pointwise.
items.note: Mathlib’s ring seminorms need not be nonarchimedean (IsNonarchimedean is separate). The statements about the trivial norm in Example 2.1.6 are immediate.

items.name: The subring o_A, the ideal m_A and κ_A
items.statement: For a submultiplicative seminorm with α(1) ≤ 1: o_A = {α ≤ 1} is a ring, m_A = {α < 1} an ideal and κ_A = o_A/m_A; for a field with a multiplicative norm these are the valuation ring, its maximal ideal and residue field. Products of power-multiplicative seminorms give power-multiplicative seminorms on the bounded part.
items.note: Mathlib has the valuation ring and residue field of a valued field, but not the unit-ball subring of a seminormed ring or the bounded part of a product.

items.name: The spectral seminorm
items.statement: For a submultiplicative α on A, α_sp(a) = lim_{s→∞} α(a^s)^{1/s} exists (Fekete) and is power-multiplicative; equivalent seminorms give the same α_sp.
items.note: Mathlib’s smoothing seminorm is KL’s α_sp; equality for equivalent seminorms follows from eq_seminorms.

items.name: Product seminorm and completed tensor product
items.statement: For bounded A → B, A → C, the product seminorm on B ⊗_A C sends f to the infimum over presentations f = Σ b_i ⊗ c_i of max β(b_i)γ(c_i); B ⊗̂_A C is the separated completion. Any submultiplicative α is equivalent to its operator seminorm α′(a) = inf{c : α(ab) ≤ cα(b)}, which satisfies α′(1) ≤ 1.
items.note: A0/R0 plan completed tensor products of Huber pairs.

items.name: Analytic fields, Banach rings and Banach algebras
items.statement: An analytic field is a field complete for a nontrivial multiplicative nonarchimedean norm; finite extensions carry a unique extension. A Banach ring is a commutative ring complete for a submultiplicative norm (the zero ring allowed); a Banach algebra over R is a Banach ring S with a bounded R → S. From §2.4 on every Banach ring is assumed to contain a topologically nilpotent unit.
items.note: There is no bundled Banach ring: it is written [NormedRing A] [CompleteSpace A] [IsUltrametricDist A]. The standing assumption of a topologically nilpotent unit from §2.4 on is a convention.

items.name: Closures of proper ideals in Banach rings
items.statement: In a Banach ring the closure of a proper ideal is proper; maximal ideals are closed.

items.name: Henselian pairs from direct limits of Banach rings
items.statement: For a direct system of Banach rings and submetric maps with limit A and infimum seminorm α: (a) (A, ker α) is henselian; (b) (o_A, m_A) is henselian. In particular (o_A, m_A) is henselian for every Banach ring A.
items.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.3 and the sentence before it, p. 28

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a completion
items.statement: With notation as in Lemma 2.2.3: (a) FÉt(A) → FÉt(Â) is rank-preserving and fully faithful; (b) if α is multiplicative and K = A/ker α is a field, FÉt(A) → FÉt(K̂) is an equivalence.
items.note: The idempotent-lifting iteration x ↦ 3x² − 2x³ and its estimates were checked.

items.name: Uniqueness of power-multiplicative extensions to finite extensions
items.statement: For K an analytic field and L/K finite, the unique multiplicative extension of the norm of K is also the unique power-multiplicative extension.

items.name: Canonical norms on finite modules over a Banach ring
items.statement: (a) For a finite R-module M, the quotient seminorms from surjections R^n → M are all equivalent. (b) An additive R-linear map from a finite R-module to a finite S-module (R → S bounded) is bounded for these seminorms.
items.note: Neither library has norms on finite modules over a normed ring; Tau Ceti’s TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology is the topological analogue over Tate rings.

items.name: Banach modules and finite Banach modules
items.statement: A Banach module over R is an R-module complete for a norm with |rv| ≤ c|r||v|; it is finite if it admits a strict surjection R^n → M (so its norm class is determined by the module). A finite R-module is a finite Banach module iff it is separated and complete for its canonical seminorm.

items.name: The open mapping theorem for Banach modules
items.statement: If R is a Banach ring with a topologically nilpotent unit, every bounded surjective homomorphism of Banach R-modules is open and strict.
items.note: Henkel; Layer 0 §0.6 plans it with Henkel’s hypotheses.

items.name: Completed tensor products over an analytic field
items.statement: For Banach modules V, W, X over an analytic field K: (a) V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective; (b) ker(f) ⊗̂_K X ≅ ker(f ⊗̂ X) for bounded f : V → W; (c) if f is strict, so is f ⊗̂ X.
items.note: Proved by reduction to separable modules with Schauder bases.

items.name: Noetherian Banach rings
items.statement: For a Banach ring R with a topologically nilpotent unit the following are equivalent: R is noetherian; every ideal of R is closed; finite Banach R-modules are the same as finite R-modules.

items.name: Banach structures on finite projective modules
items.statement: For a finite projective R-module P with P ⊕ Q ≅ R^n, the subspace and quotient norms from R^n are equivalent, make P a finite Banach module, and are independent of Q and the presentation; this defines a fully faithful section of the forgetful functor on finite projective modules. Generators e_1, …, e_n of P can be perturbed: e′_i with |e′_i − e_i| < c still generate.

items.name: Finite étale algebras as finite Banach algebras
items.statement: For B ∈ FÉt(A), the norm of Lemma 2.2.12 makes multiplication bounded, so an equivalent submultiplicative norm makes B a finite Banach A-algebra; for an adic Banach ring, B^+ is the integral closure of A^+ in B.
items.note: A1 plans the topology and plus ring on a finite étale algebra.

items.name: Tate algebras, affinoid homomorphisms and strongly noetherian Banach rings
items.statement: A{T_1/r_1, …, T_n/r_n} = {Σ a_I T^I : |a_I|r^I → 0} with the Gauss norm (submultiplicative, power-multiplicative or multiplicative with that of A); A → B is affinoid if it factors through a strict surjection A{T_1, …, T_n} → B; A is strongly noetherian if all A{T_1, …, T_n} are noetherian.

items.name: The Gel’fand spectrum M(A)
items.statement: M(A) is the set of multiplicative seminorms on A bounded by the norm, topologized as a closed subspace of ∏_a [0, |a|], hence compact; bounded maps induce continuous maps; M(Â) ≅ M(A).

items.name: Berkovich: the spectrum of a nonzero Banach ring is nonempty
items.statement: For A ≠ 0, M(A) ≠ ∅.

items.name: Ideals, the unit ideal and units via the spectrum
items.statement: Every proper ideal I has some α ∈ M(A) vanishing on I; f_1, …, f_n generate the unit ideal iff for every α some α(f_i) > 0; f is a unit iff α(f) > 0 for all α ∈ M(A).

items.name: Residue fields H(α) and the Gel’fand transform
items.statement: For α ∈ M(A), p_α = α^{−1}(0) is prime and H(α) is the completion of Frac(A/p_α); the Gel’fand transform A → ∏_α H(α) is bounded, and every maximal ideal is some p_α.

items.name: Uniform units, topologically nilpotent units and trivial spectra
items.statement: For a Banach ring A consider: (a) A is a Banach algebra over an analytic field; (b) A has a uniform unit z (topologically nilpotent with |z|_sp|z^{−1}|_sp = 1, so α(z) = |z|_sp for all α); (c) A has a topologically nilpotent unit; (d) A is free of trivial spectrum. Then (a) ⇒ (b) ⇒ (c) ⇒ (d); in characteristic p, (a) ⇔ (b); (b) ⇏ (a) in general, and (c) ⇏ (b) (k((z_1)) ⊕ k((z_2)) with incommensurable norms).

items.name: Berkovich: the spectral seminorm is the supremum over the spectrum
items.statement: The restriction of the supremum norm on ∏_{α∈M(A)} H(α) along the Gel’fand transform is the spectral seminorm of A; the supremum is attained (maximum modulus principle).

items.name: Surjectivity and fibre products via the spectrum
items.statement: A map M → N of A-modules with N finite is surjective iff it is surjective after ⊗ H(α) for all α ∈ M(A); M(B ⊗̂_A C) → M(B) ×_{M(A)} M(C) is surjective; for B faithfully finite étale over A, M(B) → M(A) is surjective (and open, Lemma 2.4.17(c)).

items.name: Closed and quotient maps from quasicompact to Hausdorff spaces
items.statement: A continuous map from a quasicompact space to a Hausdorff space is closed, so a continuous surjection (resp. bijection) between such spaces is a quotient map (resp. a homeomorphism).

items.name: Inverse limits of compact Hausdorff spaces: nonemptiness, covers and disconnections
items.statement: An inverse limit X of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces X_i is nonempty and compact; a closed subset of X_i has empty preimage in X iff it has empty preimage in some X_j; a finite open covering of X is refined by the pullback of one of some X_i; and every disconnection of X is pulled back from a disconnection of some X_j.
items.note: Mathlib has the nonemptiness (TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system), the basis of the limit topology (TopCat.isTopologicalBasis_cofiltered_limit) and the clopen statement for profinite limits only (Profinite.exists_isClopen_of_cofiltered). The argument for (e) needs the stage chosen large enough (finding E5).

items.name: Adic Banach rings
items.statement: An adic Banach ring (A, A^+) is a Banach ring A with a topologically nilpotent unit and an open, integrally closed subring A^+ ⊆ A°; morphisms are bounded maps with ϕ(A^+) ⊆ B^+; coproducts are (B ⊗̂_A C, completion of the integral closure of the image of B^+ ⊗ C^+).

items.name: Semivaluations, continuity and the adic spectrum
items.statement: A semivaluation v : A → Γ ∪ {0} satisfies v(a − b) ≤ max, v(ab) = v(a)v(b), v(0) = 0, v(1) = 1; Spv(A) is the set of equivalence classes; v is continuous if every nonzero γ in its value group bounds v near 0. Spa(A, A^+) is the set of continuous semivaluations bounded by 1 on A^+, with A^+ = {x : v(x) ≤ 1 for all v}, topologized by the sets {v(a) ≤ v(b) ≠ 0}; rational subspaces are {v(f_i) ≤ v(g) ≠ 0} with the f_i generating the unit ideal.
items.note: A misprint in the subbasic sets (finding E6).

items.name: Tate f-adic rings versus Banach rings
items.statement: Huber’s Tate rings with a topologically nilpotent unit z are Banach rings for α(x) = inf{c^n : z^{−n}x ∈ A_0}, and the categories agree up to allowing continuous (not only bounded) maps; a semivaluation bounded by 1 on A^+ is continuous iff v(z^n) < v(x) for some n whenever v(x) ≠ 0.

items.name: Huber: adic spectra are quasicompact with a basis of rational subspaces
items.statement: Spa(A, A^+) is quasicompact, and the rational subspaces form a basis of quasicompact open subsets.

items.name: Comparison maps between the Gel’fand and adic spectra
items.statement: There is a (discontinuous) injection M(A) → Spa(A, A^+); if A has a uniform unit z, v ↦ α(v)(x) = inf{|z|_sp^{r/s} : v(z^r) > v(x^s)} is a continuous retraction Spa(A, A^+) → M(A), a quotient map exhibiting M(A) as the maximal Hausdorff quotient; disconnections of the two spaces correspond, and M(A) is dense in Spa(A, A^+).

items.name: Perturbing the parameters of a rational subspace
items.statement: For a rational subspace U given by f_1, …, f_n, g, c = inf{α(g) : α ∈ image of U in M(A)} > 0, and any f′_i, g′ within ε < c of f_i, g define the same U.

items.name: Rational subspaces of M(A) and encircling
items.statement: A rational subspace of M(A) is its intersection with a rational subspace of Spa(A, A^+), {α(f_i) ≤ α(g)}; these are closed, and those that are neighbourhoods of α (encircle α) form a neighbourhood basis. Rational subspaces of Spa are not determined by their trace on M(A) in general, and Berkovich also allows radii p_i.

items.name: Adic fields and residue fields of points of Spa
items.statement: An adic field is (K, K^+) with K analytic and K^+ a valuation ring; for v ∈ Spa(A, A^+), (H(v), H(v)^+) is the adic field of the completed residue field with the valuation ring of v, and (A, A^+) → (H(v), H(v)^+) sends the unique closed point of Spa(H(v), H(v)^+) (the point given by H(v)^+) to v.
items.note: Corrected: the paper says “generic point” (finding E7, corrected in part II).

items.name: Affinoid subdomains and localizations
items.statement: A quasicompact open U ⊆ Spa(A, A^+) is an affinoid subdomain if some affinoid (A, A^+) → (B, B^+) is initial among maps whose spectrum lands in U; rational subspaces are affinoid subdomains (rational localizations), and completed tensor products of localizations correspond to intersections.

items.name: Rational localizations are explicit and homeomorphic onto their image
items.statement: The rational subspace U = {v(f_i) ≤ v(g)} is represented by B = A{T_1, …, T_n}/(closure of (gT_i − f_i)) with B^+ the completed integral closure of A^+[T]; Spa(B, B^+) → U is a homeomorphism under which rational subspaces correspond.

items.name: Rational, affinoid and strong rational coverings; the structure presheaf; sheafiness
items.statement: Rational (affinoid) coverings are finite coverings by rational (affinoid) subdomains; a strong rational covering is one whose relative interiors cover M(A). The structure presheaf O takes U to the inverse limit of the rational localizations inside U, with O(Spa(B, B^+)) = B; (A, A^+) is sheafy if O is a sheaf, equivalently B → H^0(Spa(B, B^+), O) is an isomorphism for every rational localization.

items.name: Huber: strongly noetherian adic Banach rings are sheafy
items.statement: If A is strongly noetherian then (A, A^+) is sheafy.

items.name: Stalks and Hausdorff localizations are henselian
items.statement: (a) Each stalk O_v is a henselian local ring whose residue field is dense in H(v). (b) The Hausdorff localization A_α (direct limit over rational localizations encircling α) is a henselian local ring with residue field dense in H(α). (c) For B faithfully finite étale over A, M(B) → M(A) is open.
items.note: Locality of stalks is planned in Layer 3; the henselian property and Hausdorff localizations are not.

items.name: Standard rational and standard Laurent coverings
items.statement: For f_1, …, f_n generating the unit ideal, U_i = {v(f_j) ≤ v(f_i) for all j}; for arbitrary f_i, the Laurent covering by the S_e = ∩ S_{i,e_i} with S_{i,−} = {v(f_i) ≤ 1}, S_{i,+} = {v(f_i) ≥ 1}; n = 1 gives simple Laurent coverings.

items.name: Refinement of rational coverings
items.statement: (a) Every rational covering is refined by a standard rational covering. (b) For a standard rational covering there is a standard Laurent covering on each piece of which it restricts to a standard rational covering generated by units. (c) A standard rational covering generated by units is refined by a standard Laurent covering generated by units.

items.name: Reduction of covering properties to simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: A property of rational coverings of rational subdomains that is local (passes from refinements), transitive (passes to composite coverings) and holds for simple Laurent coverings holds for all rational coverings of all rational subdomains.
items.note: Wrong cross-references in step (iv) of the proof (finding E8).

items.name: Čech acyclicity criterion
items.statement: If a presheaf of abelian groups F satisfies Ȟ^0 = F(U) and Ȟ^1 = 0 for every simple Laurent covering of every rational subdomain U, then for every rational covering V of every rational U, H^0(U, F) = Ȟ^0(U, F; V) = F(U) and H^i(U, F) = Ȟ^i(U, F; V) = 0 for i > 0.

items.name: Surjectivity for simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: For the simple Laurent covering defined by f ∈ A, with localizations B_1, B_2, B_12, the map B_1 ⊕ B_2 → B_12, (b_1, b_2) ↦ b_1 − b_2, is surjective.

items.name: Tate acyclicity for sheafy adic Banach rings
items.statement: If (A, A^+) is sheafy, then for every rational covering U, H^i(Spa(A, A^+), O) = Ȟ^i(Spa(A, A^+), O; U) = A for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0.

items.name: Reduction of properties of inclusions to simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: A property of inclusions V ⊆ U of rational subdomains that is transitive and holds for each inclusion that is part of a simple Laurent covering of U holds for all inclusions of rational subdomains.
items.note: An inclusion is stated backwards in the proof (finding E9).

items.name: Affinoid algebras over an analytic field: noetherian, excellent, Noether normalization
items.statement: For an affinoid algebra A over an analytic field K: A is noetherian and excellent, every ideal is closed, finite A-modules are canonically finite Banach modules with all A-linear maps strict; for A ≠ 0 there is a finite strict monomorphism K{T_1, …, T_n} → A; maximal ideals have residue fields finite over K and correspond bijectively to the points of M(A) with residue field finite over K.
items.note: Layer 0 plans noetherianity of K⟨X⟩ and Weierstrass division. The excellence reference is misprinted (finding E10, corrected in part II).

items.name: Spectral norm of reduced affinoid algebras and finiteness of reductions
items.statement: For A reduced the spectral seminorm is a norm equivalent to the given one; for a finite morphism A → B the induced map κ_A → κ_B (for the spectral seminorms) is finite.

items.name: Rational subdomains of adic affinoids and of Maxspec
items.statement: For an adic affinoid algebra and rational U: (a) B ≅ A{T}/(gT_i − f_i) (no closure needed); (b) U ∩ Maxspec(A) is the rational subdomain of Maxspec(A) represented by A → B; (c) A reduced ⇒ B reduced; (d) A^+ = A° ⇒ B^+ = B°; coverings of Maxspec(A) by rational subdomains are refined by rational coverings of Spa.

items.name: Gerritzen–Grauert for adic affinoids
items.statement: For an affinoid subdomain U of Maxspec(A) there is a rational covering V_1, …, V_n of Spa(A, A^+) with each U ∩ V_i a rational subdomain of V_i ∩ Maxspec(A); U is a finite union of rational subdomains.
items.note: The atlas mentions Gerritzen–Grauert only for complex comparison and modular curves.

items.name: Rational coverings detected on classical points
items.statement: If A^+ = A°, a finite collection of rational subdomains of a rational subdomain Spa(B, B^+) is a rational covering iff it covers Maxspec(B).

items.name: Rational subspaces are determined by their classical points when A^+ = A°
items.statement: If A^+ = A° (so A is reduced), no two distinct rational subspaces of Spa(A, A^+) have the same intersection with Maxspec(A).
items.note: Corrected: the printed hypothesis “A reduced” is not enough (finding E11).

items.name: Affinoid subdomains of adic affinoids and of Maxspec
items.statement: (a) For an affinoid subdomain U of Spa(A, A^+) represented by A → B, U ∩ Maxspec(A) is the affinoid subdomain of Maxspec(A) represented by A → B; (b) A reduced ⇒ B reduced; (c) A^+ = A° ⇒ B^+ = B°; if A^+ = A°, affinoid coverings are detected on Maxspec.

items.name: Flatness of affinoid localizations and faithful flatness of coverings
items.statement: Affinoid localizations of adic affinoids are flat; for an affinoid covering, A → ⊕B_i is faithfully flat, so local freeness of finite modules and étaleness of finite algebras are local on affinoid coverings.
items.note: Layer 4 plans flatness of rational localizations (Wedhorn 8.30).

items.name: Theorems of Tate and Kiehl for adic affinoids
items.statement: (a) For an affinoid covering and a finite A-module M, the Čech complex of M̃ is acyclic with H^0 = M; in particular (A, A^+) is sheafy. (b) M ↦ M̃ is a tensor equivalence between finite A-modules and coherent O-modules; A → ⊕B_i is an effective descent morphism for finite Banach modules.

items.name: Clopen subsets of an adic affinoid come from idempotents
items.statement: For U closed-open in Spa(A, A^+) there is a unique idempotent e ∈ A equal to 1 on U and 0 off U, and Spa(eA, eA^+) ≅ U; likewise for M(A).

items.name: Extension to Berkovich affinoids and to affinoid algebras over Z((z))
items.statement: The results of §2.5 other than Noether normalization extend to Berkovich affinoid algebras (by base change to an analytic field with prescribed transcendentals), and to affinoid algebras over Z((z)) with the norm of Remark 2.5.23 (strongly noetherian), including flatness, faithful flatness, Tate’s theorem and idempotents.

items.name: Affinoid systems and completed direct limits
items.statement: An affinoid system is a directed system of adic affinoid algebras over Z((z)) with submetric maps; its completed direct limit is the completion of the colimit ring for the infimum seminorm, with plus ring the colimit of the A_i^+. Every adic Banach algebra is the completed direct limit of an affinoid system.
items.note: The plus rings in the proof must be integrally closed (finding E12).

items.name: Adic spectra of completed direct limits
items.statement: Spa(R, R^+) is homeomorphic to lim Spa(A_i, A_i^+), every rational subspace, rational localization and rational covering is defined at a finite stage (and encircling can be tested there), and colimits of stalks and of Hausdorff localizations are local rings with dense residue fields.

items.name: Clopen subsets of adic spectra come from idempotents
items.statement: For any adic Banach algebra (R, R^+) and U closed-open in Spa(R, R^+), there is a unique idempotent e ∈ R equal to 1 on U and 0 off U, and Spa(eR, eR^+) ≅ U.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over completed direct limits
items.statement: For an affinoid system with direct limit (A, α), I = ker α and R the completion, FÉt(A) → FÉt(A/I) → FÉt(R) are tensor equivalences.

items.name: Descent of finite étale algebras along rational coverings
items.statement: For an adic Banach algebra (R, R^+) and a rational covering {(R, R^+) → (R_i, R_i^+)}, R → R_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ R_n is an effective descent morphism for finite étale algebras over Banach rings, and hence (Remark 1.4.3) for étale Z_p-local systems.

items.name: Factorization of matrices near the identity
items.statement: If R_1 → S, R_2 → S are bounded and R_1 ⊕ R_2 → S is strict surjective, there is c > 0 such that every U ∈ GL_n(S) with |U − 1| < c is ψ(U_1)ψ(U_2) with U_i ∈ GL_n(R_i); if the sum map is almost optimal, c = 1.
items.note: A constant is off in the proof (finding E13).

items.name: Glueing squares of Banach rings
items.statement: A commutative square R → R_1, R_2 → R_12 of Banach rings is a glueing square if 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 is strict exact, R_2 → R_12 has dense image and M(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → M(R) is surjective.

items.name: Glueing finite projective modules over a glueing square
items.statement: For a finite glueing datum over a glueing square, M ⊗_R R_i → M_i and M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12 are surjective; for a finite projective glueing datum, M = ker(M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12) is finite projective and M ⊗_R R_i ≅ M_i.
items.note: The matrix identity in the proof of Lemma 2.7.4 was checked.

items.name: Tate sheaf property and Kiehl glueing property
items.statement: A presheaf of topological rings R on Spa(A, A^+) has the Tate sheaf property if every rational covering of every rational subdomain is acyclic with H^0 = R(U) (enough for simple Laurent coverings), and the Kiehl glueing property if on every rational subdomain finite projective R(U)-modules are equivalent to locally free R-modules of finite rank.

items.name: Kiehl glueing for vector bundles on sheafy adic Banach rings
items.statement: For a sheafy adic Banach ring (A, A^+), the structure sheaf satisfies the Tate sheaf property and the Kiehl glueing property: vector bundles on Spa(A, A^+) are the same as finite projective A-modules.
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans coherent sheaves on noetherian adic spaces only.

items.name: Uniform Banach rings
items.statement: A Banach ring A is uniform if its norm is equivalent to a power-multiplicative norm, equivalently to its spectral seminorm, equivalently |x²| ≥ c|x|² for some c > 0. Uniform rings are reduced, A° is bounded in them, reduced affinoid algebras are uniform, and Tate algebras over uniform rings are uniform. Boundedness of A° alone does not imply uniformity, unless A has a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z||z^{−1}| = 1.
items.note: Corrected (finding E14, corrected in part II). Layer 4 §4.2 uses Hansen–Kedlaya’s topological definition (A° bounded), which the norm-level definition refines.

items.name: Spectral norms and injectivity for uniform rings
items.statement: For A uniform: bounded maps of uniform rings are submetric for the spectral norms, isometric iff surjective on M; for a uniform adic Banach ring, A → H^0(Spa(A, A^+), O) is injective.

items.name: Projectivity of modules over uniform Banach rings by continuity of rank
items.statement: For A uniform and M finitely generated, the following are equivalent: M is projective; the rank function β ↦ dim_{H(β)} M ⊗ H(β) is continuous on M(A); M ⊗_A B is projective for some bounded A → B of uniform rings with M(B) → M(A) surjective.

items.name: Stable uniformity and its failures
items.statement: Completed tensor products and rational localizations of uniform rings need not be uniform (Q_p → C_p ⊗̂ C_p; Mihara’s example); (A, A^+) is stably uniform if all rational localizations are uniform. Scalar extension by a W(ℓ)[1/p] over W(k)[1/p] preserves uniformity, and (stable) uniformity descends along A → A ⊗̂_K L and along bounded maps that split as Banach modules; sheafy rings covered by stably uniform ones are stably uniform.
items.note: Layer 4 §4.2 plans stable uniformity; the descent and extension statements are part of the route. A misprint ends the proof of Lemma 2.8.6 (finding E15).

items.name: Mihara: closedness of principal ideals over a uniform ring
items.statement: For A uniform and f ∈ A, the ideals (T − f), (1 − fT) of A{T} and A{T, T^{−1}} are closed (multiplication by T − f is isometric for the spectral norm).

items.name: Laurent exactness and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem
items.statement: For a uniform adic Banach ring and the simple Laurent covering by f, 0 → A → B_1 ⊕ B_2 → B_12 → 0 is exact; hence a stably uniform adic Banach ring is sheafy.
items.note: A self-citation in the proof of 2.8.9 (finding E16).

items.name: Uniformization
items.statement: The separated completion A^u of A for the spectral seminorm is uniform, M(A^u) ≅ M(A), and A ↦ A^u (with A^{u+} the completed image of A^+) is left adjoint to the inclusion of uniform (adic) Banach rings; Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ≅ Spa(A, A^+) matching rational subspaces.
items.note: A0 plans the uniformization and its universal property.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a Banach ring and over its uniformization
items.statement: For A uniform and B ∈ FÉt(A) there is a maximal power-multiplicative seminorm on B bounding A → B; B ⊗ A_i is monogenic on a strong rational covering; FÉt(A) → FÉt(A^u) is a tensor equivalence, and the maximal seminorm makes each B ∈ FÉt(A^u) a uniform Banach algebra with norm equivalent to that of Definition 2.2.14. If A^+ = A°, then B^+ = B°.
items.note: Misprints in Lemmas 2.8.14–2.8.15 and the proof of Proposition 2.8.16 (findings E17–E19).

items.name: Perfect F_p-algebras and the perfect closure
items.statement: An F_p-algebra R is perfect if Frobenius x ↦ x^p is bijective (so R is reduced; localizations of perfect rings are perfect). The perfect closure R^perf is the direct limit of R → R → ⋯ along Frobenius; R → R^perf identifies the reduced quotient of R with a subring. For any set X, R[X]^perf ≅ R^perf[X^{p^{−∞}}] naturally in R.
items.note: Perfect implies reduced is stated as the vanishing of the p-nilradical; Example 3.1.14 is the universal property PerfectClosure.lift applied to R[X].

items.name: Perfect uniform (adic) Banach F_p-algebras
items.statement: A perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra is a uniform Banach ring of characteristic p whose underlying ring is perfect; in the adic case R^+ is then perfect because it is integrally closed. A power-multiplicative seminorm on R extends uniquely to R^perf, giving homeomorphisms M(R^perf) ≅ M(R) and Spa(R^perf, R^{+,perf}) ≅ Spa(R, R^+).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P1 plans the characteristic-p case of perfectoid Tate rings (perfect complete uniform Tate rings).

items.name: Frobenius-fixed elements of a perfect ring are F_p-combinations of idempotents
items.statement: If R is perfect and e^p = e, then e_i = ∏_{j ≠ i}(e − j)/(i − j) (i ∈ F_p) are idempotents with e = Σ i e_i. Hence R^{ϕ=1} is the F_p-algebra generated by the idempotents of R, and equals F_p iff R is connected.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a perfect ring are perfect
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra, every S ∈ FÉt(R) is perfect.

items.name: Strict maps, tensor products and quotients of perfect uniform Banach algebras
items.statement: For perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebras: (a) a strict homomorphism is almost optimal (not necessarily optimal); (b) if f_1 − f_2 is strict it is almost optimal; (c) completed tensor products R ⊗̂_T S are again perfect uniform (unlike general uniform rings); (d) the quotient by a closed perfect ideal is perfect uniform.

items.name: Rational localizations of perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebras
items.statement: Every rational localization of a perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebra (R, R^+) is again perfect uniform, so (R, R^+) is stably uniform. Explicitly, the localization is the quotient of the completed perfection of R{T_1, …, T_n} by the closed ideal generated by the (gT_i − f_i)^{p^{−h}}, and for any c > 1 the quotient norm from R{T} can be taken within a factor c of the spectral norm.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P2 plans perfectoid rational localizations; in characteristic p these are the perfect uniform ones.

items.name: Finite perfect algebras over a perfect uniform Banach algebra are uniform
items.statement: If R is perfect uniform and S is a finite perfect R-algebra that is a finite Banach R-module (e.g. S ∈ FÉt(R)), then S is a perfect uniform Banach algebra. An isometric automorphism of R that extends to S ∈ FÉt(R) is isometric on S.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans that finite étale algebras over a perfectoid ring are perfectoid; Lemma 3.1.9 is the characteristic-p case. The isometry statement of Lemma 3.1.10 is a small addition.

items.name: Integral elements of finite étale algebras over perfect uniform algebras are almost finite étale
items.statement: For R perfect uniform over a perfect analytic field L and S ∈ FÉt(R), o_S is perfect with Ω_{o_S/o_R} = 0, and the quotient of o_S by the sum of its finitely generated projective o_R-submodules is killed by m_L; o_S need not be finite over o_R.

items.name: Tate acyclicity and Kiehl glueing for perfect uniform adic Banach algebras
items.statement: For f ∈ R and the rational subdomains {v(f) ≤ 1}, {v(f) ≥ 1}, {v(f) = 1}, the sequence 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 is almost optimal exact (Lemma 3.1.12). Hence every perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebra is sheafy and satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties (Theorem 3.1.13).

items.name: Finite étale algebras are unchanged by perfection
items.statement: (a) For any F_p-algebra R, base change FÉt(R) → FÉt(R^perf) is a tensor equivalence. (b) If R is a uniform Banach F_p-algebra and S is the completion of R^perf, then FÉt(R) → FÉt(S) is a tensor equivalence.
items.note: Mathlib has the topological half (PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap applies to R → R^perf) and the category CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale, but not the equivalence.

items.name: Sheafy adic Banach F_p-algebras that are locally perfect uniform are perfect
items.statement: If (A, A^+) is a sheafy adic Banach F_p-algebra admitting a rational covering by perfect uniform algebras, then A is perfect. This is essentially Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Corollary 10, with sheafy in place of stably uniform; without uniformity the covering conjecture fails (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Proposition 13).
items.note: Remarks 3.1.17 and 3.6.27 cite the covering conjecture from the wrong paper (findings E20, E36).

items.name: Strict p-rings and the universal property of W(R)
items.statement: A strict p-ring is a p-torsion-free p-adically complete ring S with S/(p) perfect. For p-adically complete U, every ring map S/(p) → U/(p) lifts uniquely to a multiplicative map t: S/(p) → U (t(x) ≡ y^{p^n} mod p^{n+1} for y lifting the image of x^{p^{−n}}); in particular S has a Teichmüller section [·], every x ∈ S is uniquely Σ p^n [x_n], and Σ p^n [x_n] ↦ Σ p^n t(x_n) is a ring homomorphism S → U (Lemma 3.2.2). The addition law is given by universal homogeneous polynomials P_n in p-power roots (Remark 3.2.3). S ↦ S/(p) is an equivalence from strict p-rings to perfect F_p-algebras (Theorem 3.2.4).
items.locator: §3.2, Definition 3.2.1, Lemma 3.2.2, Remark 3.2.3 and Theorem 3.2.4, pp. 71–73
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 plans W(R) for perfect R with its Teichmüller representatives and p-adically complete universal property. Mathlib has pieces: the multiplicative lift Perfection.teichmuller, uniqueness of maps agreeing on Teichmüller lifts (WittVector.eq_of_apply_teichmuller_eq) and θ as a special case, but no notion of strict p-ring and no general lifting theorem.

items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect ring
items.statement: For R perfect, W(R), the p-typical Witt vectors, is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with W(R)/(p) ≅ R, every element is Σ p^n [x_n] with x_n ∈ R, and Frobenius lifts to an automorphism ϕ of W(R); W_n(R) = W(R)/(p^n) is the ring of truncated Witt vectors.
items.note: Mathlib proves existence of the Teichmüller expansion; its uniqueness follows from p-torsion-freeness and W(R)/(p) ≅ R. W_n(R) ≅ W(R)/(p^n) follows from WittVector.mem_ker_truncate and WittVector.mem_span_p_pow_iff_le_coeff_eq_zero.

items.name: ϕ-modules over W_n(R) acquire invariant bases over a faithfully finite étale cover
items.statement: Let R be perfect, n ≥ 1, and M a finite projective W_n(R)-module of everywhere positive rank with a semilinear ϕ^a-action. Some faithfully finite étale R-algebra S makes M ⊗ W_n(S) admit a ϕ^a-fixed basis; a fixed basis modulo p^m (m < n) can be lifted. The proof represents invariant bases by the closed-open part of the scheme of invariant n-tuples.
items.note: The representing ring is corrected in the authors’ errata (finding E21).

items.name: Lisse Z/p^n-sheaves on a perfect ring and ϕ-modules over W_n(R)
items.statement: For R perfect and n ≥ 1 there is a tensor equivalence, natural in R and n, between lisse sheaves of Z/p^nZ-modules on Spec R and finite projective W_n(R)-modules with a semilinear ϕ-action.
items.note: The inverse functor’s formula is corrected in the authors’ errata (finding E22).

items.name: Lang torsors for unipotent Witt group schemes
items.statement: For d, m ≥ 1, n ≥ 2 (n = 1 allowed if p > 2), an algebraic Lie subalgebra g of gl_d(Q_p), g_n = g ∩ gl_d(p^n Z_p), and G_{n,m} the unipotent group scheme of g_n ⊗ Z/p^m (Greenberg realization over F_p): for perfect R, ϕ-conjugacy classes G_{n,m}(R)/∼ (g_1 ∼ h^{−1}g_1ϕ(h)) are in natural bijection with H^1_et(R, G_{n,m}(F_p)). For general group schemes Hilbert 90 can fail (Serre, Grothendieck on special groups).

items.name: Direct perfection of a ring with a Frobenius lift
items.statement: For A p-torsion-free with A/pA reduced, an endomorphism ϕ_A lifting the p^r-power Frobenius, and (A/pA)^perf ≅ R, there is a map s_ϕ: A → W(R) with ϕ^r ∘ s_ϕ = s_ϕ ∘ ϕ_A, identifying W(R) with the p-adic completion of the direct limit of A along ϕ_A. For A = Z[T], ϕ(T) = T^p it sends T to [T̄] but s_ϕ(T + 1) ≠ [T̄ + 1].
items.note: PrismaticCohomology PR.0 plans Frobenius lifts on p-torsion-free rings and completed perfection.

items.name: Frobenius-stable finitely generated ideals of a perfect ring are idempotent
items.statement: If R is perfect and J is a finitely generated ideal with ϕ(J) = J, then J is generated by an idempotent; in particular R/J is finite projective over R.

items.name: ϕ-modules over W_n(R) flat over Z/p^n are projective
items.statement: For R perfect, a finitely presented W_n(R)-module that is flat over Z/p^nZ and carries a semilinear ϕ-action is finite projective over W_n(R).

items.name: The Gauss seminorms λ(α) on W(R) and the restriction μ(β)
items.statement: For R perfect and α a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm on R bounded by the trivial norm, λ(α)(Σ p^i [x_i]) = sup_i p^{−i} α(x_i) is a seminorm of the same kind on W(R) bounded by the p-adic norm; conversely μ(β)(x) = β([x]). The maps λ: M(R) → M(W(R)) and μ: M(W(R)) → M(R) are continuous, μ ∘ λ = id and λ ∘ μ ≥ id (Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Lemmas 4.1–4.2).

items.name: Primitive elements of degree 1
items.statement: For R complete for a power-multiplicative norm α bounded by the trivial norm, z = Σ p^i [z_i] ∈ W(R) is primitive of degree 1 if α(x z_0) = p^{−1} α(x) for all x ∈ R and z_1 ∈ R^× (equivalently z − [z_0] ∈ pW(R)^×); then (z) is closed, and R[z_0^{−1}] is a Banach algebra over F_p((z_0)). The condition is stronger than Fargues–Fontaine’s α(z_0) < 1. From §3.6 on the reduction z_0 must also be a unit of R (authors’ errata).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P1 plans primitive degree-one ideals and the classification of marked untilts (finding E23).

items.name: A primitive element of degree 1 from p-power roots of unity
items.statement: If R is uniform with spectral norm α and π ∈ R^× has α(π) = p^{−p/(p−1)} and α(π^{−1}) = p^{p/(p−1)}, then z = Σ_{i=0}^{p−1} [π + 1]^{i/p} has z_0 = π^{(p−1)/p}, α(z_0) = p^{−1}, and z_1 a unit; so z is primitive of degree 1.
items.note: The cyclotomic test case of PerfectoidSpaces P1.

items.name: Reduced representatives modulo a primitive element
items.statement: If R is complete for a power-multiplicative norm α and z ∈ W(o_R) is primitive of degree 1, every x ∈ W(o_R) is congruent modulo z to some y = Σ p^i [y_i] with α(y_0) ≥ α(y_i) for all i > 0.

items.name: Quotient norms modulo a primitive element and the spectrum of W(o_R)/(z)
items.statement: (a) For γ a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm on o_R bounded by the trivial norm, the quotient seminorm σ(γ) on W(o_R)/(z) induced by λ(γ) is of the same kind and μ(σ(γ)) = γ. (b) σ is a continuous section of μ inducing a homeomorphism M(o_R) ≅ M(W(o_R)/(z)) that matches rational subspaces. (c) It induces a homeomorphism M(R) ≅ M(W(o_R)[[z_0]^{−1}]/(z)) matching rational subspaces.
items.note: P1 plans the untilt construction with its topology; P2 plans the tilting homeomorphism of spectra, including the rank-one case.

items.name: Untilts of a perfect analytic field
items.statement: For L a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and z ∈ W(o_L) primitive of degree 1, F = W(o_L)[[z_0]^{−1}]/(z) is an analytic field with valuation ring W(o_L)/(z) and the same residue field, and o_L/(z_0) ≅ o_F/(p), so Frobenius is surjective on o_F/(p) and F is not discretely valued. Examples: the completions of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}) and of Q_p(p^{p^{−∞}}).

items.name: Approximation modulo a primitive element with small higher Witt components
items.statement: For R, z as above, ε > 0 and m ≥ 0, every x ∈ W(o_R)[[z_0]^{−1}] is congruent modulo z to some y = Σ p^n [y_n] with α(y_1) ≤ max{p^{−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}} α(y_0), ε} and α(y_n) ≤ max{α(y_0), ε} (n > 1) for every α ∈ M(R).

items.name: Inverse perfection
items.statement: For a ring A, A^♭ = lim(⋯ → A/pA → A/pA) along Frobenius is a perfect F_p-algebra, and A^♭ → A/pA is surjective when Frobenius is surjective on A/pA. For A p-adically complete, reduction gives a multiplicative isomorphism lim_{x ↦ x^p} A ≅ A^♭ (Remark 3.4.10).

items.name: Inverse perfection only depends on A modulo a nilpotent thickening of (p)
items.statement: If I is an ideal of A with I^m ⊆ (p) ⊆ I for some m, then A^♭ → (A/I)^♭ is an isomorphism.
items.note: P1 plans the tilt and its integral descriptions, where R^♭ is computed modulo any pseudouniformizer dividing p.

items.name: Fontaine’s map θ
items.statement: From A^♭ → A/pA one gets a multiplicative map x ↦ x^♯, A^♭ → Â (the p-adic completion), and a homomorphism θ: W(A^♭) → Â with θ([x]) = x^♯ whose reduction modulo p is the projection A^♭ → A/pA; so θ is surjective iff Frobenius is surjective on A/pA.
items.note: Mathlib builds θ for a p-adically complete ring in which p is not a unit; Â is one, with Â/p = A/p. surjective_fontaineTheta is the direction used; the converse is read off mk_fontaineTheta.

items.name: Norms on the inverse perfection
items.statement: For A p-adically separated and β a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm bounded by the p-adic norm, α = μ(θ^*(β)) is such a seminorm on A^♭ bounded by the trivial norm, and θ is bounded for λ(α) and β. If β is a power-multiplicative (multiplicative) norm and A is complete, α is a norm of the same kind and A^♭ is complete.
items.note: P1 plans the tilt’s completeness, uniformity and integral subrings.

items.name: Density passes to inverse perfections
items.statement: Let A_1 = ∪ A_{1,i} be p-adically separated with Frobenius surjective on each A_{1,i}/p, A_2 p-adically separated with a norm β_2 bounded by the p-adic norm, ψ: A_1 → A_2 a homomorphism and α_2 = μ(θ^*(β_2)). (a) If ψ has dense image, so does ∪ A_{1,i}^♭ → A_2^♭. (b) If the image is dense in m_{A_2}, the image of ψ^♭ is dense in m_{A_2^♭}.

items.name: The kernel of θ is generated by a primitive element
items.statement: Let A be p-adically separated, p-torsion-free and complete for a power-multiplicative norm bounded by the p-adic norm, and suppose z ∈ W(A^♭) is primitive of degree 1 with θ(z) = 0. For θ extended to W(A^♭)[[z_0]^{−1}] → A[θ([z_0])^{−1}]: (a) ker θ = (z); (b) θ is optimal; (c) Frobenius is surjective on A/(p) iff θ has dense image. For R perfect, W(R)^♭ ≅ R and θ: W(W(R)^♭) → W(R) is an isomorphism (Remark 3.4.6). Surjectivity of Frobenius on A/pA passes to A/I when I^m ⊆ (p) ⊆ I, but not conversely (Z_p[√p]); a partial converse holds.
items.note: P1 plans θ, its surjectivity and the principal description of its kernel.

items.name: Perfectoid analytic fields
items.statement: An analytic field F is perfectoid if it has characteristic 0, residue characteristic p, is not discretely valued, and Frobenius is surjective on o_F/(p).

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid field
items.statement: For F perfectoid with norm β, R = (o_F/(p))^♭ and α = μ(θ^*(β)): (a) K = Frac(R) is a perfect analytic field of characteristic p with o_K = R; (b) β(F^×) = α(K^×); (c) for z_0 ∈ K with α(z_0) = p^{−1}, o_F/(p) ≅ o_K/(z_0) naturally, so κ_F ≅ κ_K; (d) ker θ contains a primitive element of degree 1, which generates the kernel of θ: W(o_K)[[z_0]^{−1}] → F.
items.note: Mathlib has the field Tilt = Frac(PreTilt O p) with the valuation PreTilt.val, but not its completeness, value group or residue field.

items.name: The perfectoid correspondence for fields
items.statement: F ↦ (Frac((o_F/(p))^♭), ker θ) and (L, I) ↦ Frac(W(o_L)/I) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid analytic fields and pairs (L, I) with L a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and I a principal ideal of W(o_L) generated by a primitive element of degree 1.

items.name: Finite extensions correspond with the same degree
items.statement: If F and (L, I) correspond and M/L is finite, then (M, I W(o_M)) corresponds to a finite extension E/F with [E : F] = [M : L]. The proof uses Artin’s lemma, which needs the Galois group to act faithfully on E.
items.note: The faithfulness check is added in the authors’ errata (finding E24).

items.name: Untilts of algebraically closed fields are algebraically closed
items.statement: If F and (L, I) correspond and L is algebraically closed, then so is F; the proof builds a root of any monic P ∈ o_F[T] by successive approximation, solving the reduced equation in o_L/(z) ≅ o_F/(p).

items.name: Tilting of finite étale algebras over perfectoid fields
items.statement: For corresponding F and (L, I), the correspondence of Lemma 3.5.4 gives a tensor equivalence FÉt(F) ≅ FÉt(L); every finite extension of F is perfectoid and the absolute Galois groups of F and L are homeomorphic. Forgetting I, the functor F ↦ L is not fully faithful.

items.name: Vanishing of H^1(G, 1 + m_K) for finite isometric actions
items.statement: If K is a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and a finite group G acts faithfully on K by isometries, then H^1(G, 1 + m_K) = 0. The additive cochain complex of K is almost optimal exact (normal basis theorem and Frobenius), and a multiplicative cocycle is trivialized by successive approximation.

items.name: Perfectoid fields descend along finite extensions
items.statement: If E/F is a finite extension of analytic fields with E perfectoid, then F is perfectoid. After enlarging E to be Galois with group G, one finds a G-invariant primitive generator of the ideal I of the tilt L, and the fixed field of L gives F.
items.note: Findings E25–E26 concern the proof.

items.name: Perfectoid fields are deeply ramified
items.statement: An analytic field K is deeply ramified if Ω_{o_L/o_K} = 0 for every finite extension L/K. Every perfectoid field is deeply ramified (the converse is Gabber–Ramero, Proposition 6.6.6).

items.name: Perfectoid uniform adic Banach Q_p-algebras
items.statement: A uniform adic Banach Q_p-algebra (A, A^+) is perfectoid if Frobenius is surjective on A^+/(p) and some x ∈ A^+ has x^p ≡ p mod p^2A^+; a uniform Banach algebra A is perfectoid if (A, A°) is. This agrees with Fontaine’s definition for uniform Banach Q_p-algebras; Fontaine’s notion also covers perfect uniform F_p-algebras and rings over neither.

items.name: Equivalent formulations of the perfectoid condition
items.statement: For (A, A^+) uniform over an analytic field F ⊇ Q_p: (a) if |F^×| ≠ |Q_p^×|, perfectoid iff Frobenius is surjective on A^+/(p); (b) F is perfectoid as an algebra iff as a field; (c) with the spectral norm, A is perfectoid iff for some (equivalently every) c ∈ (p^{−1}, 1) every x has y with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|; (d) A is perfectoid iff (A, A^+) is; (e) A is perfectoid iff some topologically nilpotent unit ϖ has ϖ^p | p in A^+ and Frobenius A^+/(ϖ) → A^+/(ϖ^p) surjective.

items.name: θ is surjective for perfectoid algebras, with primitive kernel
items.statement: For (A, A^+) perfectoid, θ: W(A^{+,♭}) → A^+ is surjective and its kernel is generated by an element primitive of degree 1.

items.name: The tilt and untilt functors
items.statement: For (A, A^+) perfectoid with ker θ = (z): R(A) = A^{+,♭}[z_0^{−1}], R^+(A^+) = A^{+,♭}, I(A, A^+) = ker θ. For ((R, R^+), I) with I generated by a primitive z: A(R, I) = (W(R^+)/I)[p^{−1}], A^+(R^+, I) = W(R^+)/I; W(R^+)[[z_0]^{−1}] → A(R, I) is optimal. Both constructions preserve idempotents, so Spec R and Spec A have the same clopen subsets (not the same irreducible components).
items.note: The authors’ errata add the argument that R^+(A^+) is a ring of integral elements of R(A) (finding E27).

items.name: The perfectoid correspondence for Banach algebras
items.statement: A ↦ (R(A), I(A)) and (R, I) ↦ A(R, I) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebras and pairs (R, I) with R perfect uniform Banach over F_p and I ⊂ W(o_R) principal, generated by a primitive element of degree 1; likewise for adic Banach algebras with pairs ((R, R^+), I), I ⊂ W(R^+). The algebras need not lie over a perfectoid field.

items.name: Perfectoid Tate algebras
items.statement: For corresponding A and (R, I) and r_1, …, r_n > 0, the completions B, S of A{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}] and R{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}] for the weighted Gauss norm are perfectoid and perfect, and B corresponds to (S, I W(o_S)) with (T_i, T_i^{1/p}, …) ↦ T_i.
items.note: A test case of PerfectoidSpaces P1 (perfected Tate balls).

items.name: Approximation by p-th powers in perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For A perfectoid with spectral norm, ε > 0, m ≥ 0 and x ∈ A, there is y = θ([y_0]) with β(x − y^p) ≤ max{p^{−1−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}} β(x), ε} for all β ∈ M(A); in particular |x − y^p| ≤ p^{−1−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}}|x|. The constant cannot be improved to p^{−p/(p−1)} (Kedlaya, Example 5.9).

items.name: Strict morphisms under tilting
items.statement: With spectral norms: (a) if ψ̄: R → S is strict, the untilted ψ: A → B is almost optimal, and surjective if ψ̄ is; (b) if ψ̄_1 − ψ̄_2 is strict surjective, ψ_1 − ψ_2 is almost optimal and surjective; (c) a strict homomorphism ψ of perfectoid algebras is almost optimal and ψ(A) is perfectoid; (d) then the tilt ψ̄ is almost optimal, and surjective if ψ is. Strict surjectivity does not imply surjectivity on integral elements.
items.note: Findings E28–E29 correct the statement of (a) and a bound in the proof of (d).

items.name: Completed tensor products of perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For morphisms A → B, A → C of perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with tilts R, S, T, the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C (tensor product norm) is the perfectoid algebra corresponding to S ⊗̂_R T; likewise for adic Banach algebras.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P2 plans fibre products of perfectoid spaces and their compatibility with tilting. The proof in the paper is incomplete; the authors correct it in part II, Theorem 3.3.13 (finding E30).

items.name: Tilting identifies adic spectra and rational localizations
items.statement: For corresponding (A, A^+) and ((R, R^+), I): (a) the homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(R) lifts to a functorial homeomorphism Spa(A, A^+) ≅ Spa(R, R^+); (b) the rational subspace defined by f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ R corresponds to the one defined by θ([f_i]), θ([g]), and every rational subspace of Spa(A, A^+) has this form; (c) corresponding rational localizations are perfectoid and correspond. The proof uses the explicit presentations A{T}/(T − g), A{U}/(Ug − 1) (Lemma 3.6.13) and strict presentations with quotient norm within any c > 1 of the spectral norm (Remark 3.6.16).
items.note: Finding E31 corrects a display in the proof.

items.name: Perfectoid adic Banach algebras are stably uniform and sheafy
items.statement: Every perfectoid adic Banach algebra is stably uniform and sheafy, and so satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties.
items.note: Finding E32 is a typo in the proof.

items.name: Dense-image morphisms under tilting
items.statement: (a) If ψ̄: R → S is a bounded homomorphism of uniform Banach F_p-algebras with dense image and R is perfect, then S is perfect and the untilt ψ: A → B has dense image. (b) If A is perfectoid and ψ: A → B is a bounded homomorphism with dense image to a uniform Banach Q_p-algebra, then B is perfectoid and the tilt has dense image. (c) In both cases ψ̄ is surjective iff ψ is.
items.note: Finding E33 corrects a symbol in the proof.

items.name: Uniform completed tensor products over any base are perfectoid
items.statement: If C → A and C → B are bounded homomorphisms of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with A and B perfectoid, the uniform completion (A ⊗̂_C B)^u is perfectoid.

items.name: Completion of a perfectoid algebra along an ideal containing p
items.statement: For A perfectoid with its spectral norm and J a finitely generated ideal of o_A containing p, the inverse limit R of the o_A/J^n (quotient norms, supremum norm) gives B = R[p^{−1}], which is again a perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebra.
items.note: The proof in the paper does not show that B is uniform; the authors correct it in part II, Theorem 3.3.18(v) (finding E34).

items.name: Finite étale algebras over perfectoid algebras correspond (almost purity)
items.statement: For corresponding A and (R, I): the untilt of S ∈ FÉt(R) lies in FÉt(A) with norm equivalent to any Banach norm on it (Lemma 3.6.20); every B ∈ FÉt(A), with a Banach norm from Proposition 2.8.16, is perfectoid, and FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(R) as tensor categories, so Ω_{o_B/o_A} = 0 (Theorem 3.6.21). Consequently the small étale sites of the associated adic spaces agree (Scholze).

items.name: Perfectoid algebras descend along faithfully finite étale maps
items.statement: Let A → B be a morphism of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with B perfectoid. (a) If A → B is faithfully finite étale, A is perfectoid. (b) If k ⊆ ℓ are perfect fields, K = W(k)[p^{−1}], L = W(ℓ)[p^{−1}], A is a Banach K-algebra and B = (A ⊗̂_K L)^u, then A ⊗̂_K L = B and A is perfectoid.
items.note: Finding E35 updates a citation in the proof.

items.name: The multiplicative inverse limit of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: (a) For corresponding A and (R, I), x ↦ (θ([x]), θ([x^{1/p}]), …) is an isomorphism R ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} A. (b) For A perfectoid, lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense Z-subalgebra of A. (c) If A is uniform over a perfectoid B and lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense B-subalgebra, A is perfectoid.
items.note: P1 plans the multiplicative inverse limit defining the tilt.

items.name: Perfectoid Kummer covers of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras
items.statement: Let A be uniform over Q_p and U ⊆ m_A generate a dense Q_p-subalgebra. The completed direct limit B of the finite étale algebras B_{T,n} = A[x_{t,n}]/(x_{t,n}^{p^n} − 1 − t : t ∈ T) ⊗ Q_p(μ_{p^n}) (spectral seminorms) is a perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebra, M(B) → M(A) is surjective, and A → B is isometric.

items.name: Preperfectoid, strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid algebras
items.statement: A uniform Banach Q_p-algebra A is preperfectoid if A ⊗̂_{Q_p} K is uniform and perfectoid for some perfectoid field K (Scholze–Weinstein), strongly preperfectoid if for every perfectoid field K, and relatively perfectoid if A ⊗̂_{Q_p} B is uniform and perfectoid for every perfectoid algebra B; likewise for adic Banach algebras. The completed perfected Tate algebra Q_p{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}]^∧ is relatively perfectoid; perfectoid algebras are generally not preperfectoid.
items.note: Finding E37 corrects a letter in the definition.

items.name: Uniformity, rational localizations and sheafiness of preperfectoid algebras
items.statement: If A is preperfectoid then A ⊗̂_{Q_p} B is uniform for every uniform Banach Q_p-algebra B (Proposition 3.7.3). Every rational localization of a preperfectoid (A, A^+) is preperfectoid, so (A, A^+) is stably uniform, sheafy, and satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties (Theorem 3.7.4).
items.note: Finding E38 concerns the proof of Theorem 3.7.4.

items.name: Finite étale algebras and tensor products of preperfectoid algebras
items.statement: If A is preperfectoid, every B ∈ FÉt(A) (with its Banach norm) is preperfectoid (Proposition 3.7.5). Completed tensor products of strongly preperfectoid (resp. relatively perfectoid) adic Banach algebras over Q_p are strongly preperfectoid (resp. relatively perfectoid) (Proposition 3.7.6); the argument fails for preperfectoid algebras.

items.name: Robba rings, bounded and integral Robba rings, the Amice field and their topologies
items.statement: Let K = Frac(W(k)) for a perfect field k of characteristic p, with the p-adic norm and the Witt Frobenius φ_K, and fix ω ∈ (0, 1). For r > 0, ℛ_K^r is the ring of Laurent series Σ_{i∈ℤ} c_i T^i (c_i ∈ K) with |c_i|ρ^i → 0 as i → ±∞ for every ρ ∈ [ω^r, 1), i.e. convergent on ω^r ≤ |T| < 1; ℛ_K^{int,r} ⊂ ℛ_K^r is the subring of series with all |c_i| ≤ 1, ℛ_K^{bd,r} = ℛ_K^{int,r}[p^{−1}], and ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd, ℛ_K are the unions over r > 0. ℛ_K^int is a henselian but not complete local ring with residue field k((T̄)); the completion of the field ℛ_K^bd is the Amice field ℰ_K of series with sup_i |c_i| < ∞ and |c_i| → 0 as i → −∞; and the units of ℛ_K are exactly the nonzero elements of ℛ_K^bd (Newton polygons). Rings inside ℰ_K carry the p-adic topology of the Gauss norm and the weak topology (bounded sequences converging T-adically modulo each p^n), for both of which ℰ_K is complete; rings inside ℛ_K^r carry the Fréchet topology of the ω^s-Gauss norms, s ∈ (0, r], for which ℛ_K^r is complete; ℛ_K carries the LF topology, the locally convex direct limit of the ℛ_K^r. A formal series Σ c_i T^i converges in ℰ_K for the weak (not the p-adic) topology, in ℛ_K^r for the Fréchet topology and in ℛ_K for the LF topology, and a p-adically bounded sequence in ℛ_K^{bd,r} converging for the ω^r-Gauss norm converges weakly.
items.note: RD.0 nodes robba-ring, bounded-robba-ring and units-of-robba-ring; PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations nodes robba-ring, amice-ring, bounded-robba-ring and frechet-topology (the annulus rings, Gauss norms and Fréchet and LF topologies).

items.name: Frobenius lifts, φ-modules, degree, slope and purity over the Robba rings
items.statement: A Frobenius lift on ℛ_K is an endomorphism φ(Σ c_i T^i) = Σ φ_K(c_i) u^i for some u ∈ ℛ_K^int with |u − T^p| < 1; it acts on ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd and ℰ_K, carries ℛ_K^r into ℛ_K^{r/p} for small r (not ℛ_K^r into itself), and is continuous for all the topologies above. For R ∈ {ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd, ℛ_K, 𝔬_{ℰ_K}, ℰ_K}, a φ-module over R is a finite free R-module M with an R-linear isomorphism φ^*M ≅ M. Its degree deg(M) is minus the p-adic valuation of the determinant of the matrix of φ on a basis (independent of the basis), its slope is μ(M) = deg(M)/rank(M) for M ≠ 0, and for s = c/d ∈ ℚ (d > 0) M is pure of slope s if p^c φ^d acts on some basis via a matrix U with U and U^{−1} of Gauss norm at most 1; this forces μ(M) = s, and étale means pure of slope 0 (every nonzero φ-module over ℛ_K^int or 𝔬_{ℰ_K} is étale). If M is pure of slope s, its dual is pure of slope −s. For a φ^d-module the degree is the valuation of the determinant of the matrix of φ^d divided by d, so it is unchanged on restriction to φ^{de}. This sign convention for degrees is opposite to the first author's earlier papers and agrees with geometric invariant theory (𝒪(1) has degree +1), Hartl–Pink and Fargues–Fontaine.
items.note: RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring; RD.1 nodes frobenius-module, degree-and-slope and isoclinic-frobenius-module. The RD packet follows Kedlaya's earlier convention (degree = the valuation of the determinant, semistability with reversed inequalities), so its degrees are the negatives of these; the blueprint must fix one convention.

items.name: Pure φ-modules descend from ℛ_K to ℛ_K^bd
items.statement: For each s ∈ ℚ: (a) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ_K^bd} ℰ_K is a fully faithful functor from φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd pure of slope s to φ-modules over ℰ_K pure of slope s; (b) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ_K^bd} ℛ_K is an equivalence between φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd pure of slope s and φ-modules over ℛ_K pure of slope s. Nothing is claimed for maps between pure modules of different slopes: an exact sequence 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 over ℛ_K with M_1, M_2 of rank 1 and slopes −m, m and M étale (as for trianguline representations) cannot descend to ℛ_K^bd, since there are no nonzero maps between pure φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd of different slopes.
